claims.claim: Reviewers report that controller support is broken or restricted, noting issues with non-Xbox controllers failing after short periods of play.

citations.review_text: seems to be a nice game but it completely f***ed up controller support.

I hate to leave a bad review based on controller support alone, but it is a twin stick shooter. This is one of few PC games I would prefer to play on controller, and that is the whole reason I bought the game. From what I can tell, this game only natively supports Xbox controllers. My old Xbox One controller went to the big RRoD in the sky, so I borrowed a controller from my dusty PS4 Pro. Steam's controller translation layer thingy worked great.. for 15 minutes, then forced the sticks to run me into a corner and no buttons would work except start, or whatever Sony calls that button, and the d-pad. Maybe it was a fluke, or there's an easy workaround. If so, i'll change my reccomendation. I still think it's a big oversight for a twin-stick shooter to not support a controller as common as the DualShock, even if it is inferior to Xbox controllers. I can't rightly recommend a game where you can't even make it to the 3rd floor unless you only use a controller made by Microsoft.

edit: yeah... thought it would be safe to save before 2nd floor in case something went wrong. Launch came, continue, sticks don't work thanks to Steam's busted controller input thing. I'm assuming the save is deleted as soon as loaded, which makes sense for a roguelite, to prevent savescumming, but sucks for a game where the controls break every 10 - 15 minutes if you're using Steam input. Would probably be a great game on Xbox controller or even M+KB, otherwise unplayable unless you prefer playing the first floor over and over.

I am pleased to tell you about the quality of this experience. Enter the Gungeon is a fantastic romp through ammunition ridden hell. It's a perfect roguelike to jump in casually or bust your balls with. The mechanics are rock solid (much like my member when I take rhino pills from the gas station, which are also included in the game as a secret item). The dodge rolling in particular is simple yet fundamental to survivability as it functions much like dark souls, allowing you to roll through enemy projectiles. There's a plethora of amazing guns to utilize, all providing a fresh source of damage on each run. There's tons of secret challenges (including a challenge for seeing how many rhino pills you can take before you have a heart attack, which I particularly enjoyed since it speaks to my real life experience taking various gas station rhino pills multiple times a day for approximately 10 years at this point). Even the enemies themselves resemble rhino pills to some extent, which sometimes gives me a warm wave of nostalgia upon remembering the one time I felt as though my member would explode under the sheer chemical overload of 5 rhino pills taken in the span of 2 hours. Fantastic experience, though I unfortunately must complain about the co-op as it is only done through the vessel of steam remotely or parsec, which means that if your internet is trash, good luck. In person, it's a fine game to throw on with a friend. Oh, I've also seen some people compare this game to my personal favorite roguelike (the binding of Bradly of which I've played for a total of 54 minutes last I checked) and while I can see some comparisons being apt, ultimately I would say TBOB has an infinitely more diverse selection of rhino pills present (which is why it's my favorite roguelike). That about sums up my thoughts, I will be ending this review prematurely as I believe I'm suffering from an odd arrythmia (I have no idea where it is coming from, I will be consulting my horoscope for guida…
Got catfished. Thought it was online coop. Found out it can only be done by doing play together and its borked. Person playing remotely controller couldn't move the coop player.

How hard is it to make a working multiplayer system for co-op? Extremely disappointing and this game is falsely labeled multiplayer when you are required to have two people on the same system splitting controls or using multiple controllers. Tried to play this with my friend to just end up spending half a hour looking up how to play only to find out I was misled and you can't steam remote play with both people using mouse and keyboard. Extremely stupid developers.

single_points.text: One reviewer says the game lacks a save and quit feature to interrupt a gaming session and come back to it.

citation.review_text:
Nice game, but... no, thanks.

A game that doesn't let me interrupt a gaming session and come back to it, a.k.a. a game without "save and quit", is an instant nope for me. It's sad, because the gameplay seemed promising, but I'm not 14 anymore and I want to play a game whenever I find time, not when the game allows me to.

To be clear, I'm not asking for manual saves or auto saves, just a basic "save before I quit". That doesn't clash with a rogue-like design philosophy either, it's simply a necessary feature if you want adults to buy your games, in my opinion :shrug:

single_points.text: One reviewer notes that the starting weapons were enough for the first boss, but not after that, and that second chamber bosses had phases where they just couldn't dodge projectiles.

citation.review_text:
[h1]Enter the Gungeon[/h1]

Playing this felt like I was at the edge of my seat. But I also felt like I had to be at the top of my game if I wanted to make any kind of progress. And not only that, but I couldn't make good progress without finding a proper gun. The starting weapons were enough for the first boss, but not after that. It only got worse after the 1st chamber because the 2nd chamber bosses had phases where I just couldn't dodge projectiles, even with dodging. When I couldn't deal damage fast enough, it only increased the chance of eventually dying.

I fought the Bullet King like 9 times, and I beat it perhaps 2 out of every 3 tries. I fought the Gorgun boss 7 times, and I beat it twice after I learned to shoot it when it was off-screen. I fought the Trigger Twins at least 10 times and won only a few times. I fought Gatling Gull for who knows how many times and beat it perhaps half the time.

I found lots of different weapons, most of which were on par with or only slightly better than the starting weapons. Heck Blaster was the best: it almost guaranteed getting to the 3rd chamber.

I made it to the 3rd chamber a few times, but then I got killed by shooting wagons, goop, Lead Maidens etc.

I tried different characters. The Pilot's gun was awful, so I kept playing as the Hunter.

My whole progress during my playtime was that I found a few items and a character who looked like an old woman who told me she'd help out.

It's not fun to play when you get runs where you find four locked chests in the 1st chamber but not a single key. I like using the crossbow, but then I run out of ammo and I'm left with a rusty pistol. And RNG decides how many rooms I have to clear in the 1st chamber.

I like a challenge in a game; I play most games on hard difficulty or even harder. But apparently I don't like challenge enough, because this game feels like a challenge that isn't even that interesting. It's too hard and tedious. And considering that I got the same 1st chamber …

single_points.text: One reviewer describes the game as a grindy slog where progression seems always just out of reach, complaining about the elevator dude shifting the goal posts and seeing hardly any of the guns.

citation.review_text:
This game was fun for the first few hours, but it has turned into a grindy slog where progression seems always just out of reach.  I am sick and tired of the same enemies, sick and tired of fighting the raven boss on the first floor, sick and tired of looking for secret doors, sick and tired of giving the elevator dude more and more stuff to unlock the level skip only for him to once again shift the goal posts.  This game might have 
hundreds of guns, but I am hardly seeing any of them, spending 75% of my time shooting the same starting weapons, hoping for lucky drops on the first level.  This game is too stingy and too repetitive.

single_points.text: One reviewer says your weapons are mutually exclusive, so your kit tends to stagnate later in a run, and some weapons have unintuitive mechanics that are not explained.

citation.review_text:
The goofiest roguelite. It even has couch co-op!

There are so many bizarro gun jokes, pop culture references, unique enemies, and odd secrets. The game is brutally hard, you mainly progress by learning enemy attack patterns. The story keeps giving you a reason to do "just one more run." The main theme can be played at my funeral.

My only criticisms:
- Your weapons are mutually exclusive, so your kit tends to stagnate later in a run.
- Some weapons have unintuitive mechanics that are not explained.
- The Resourceful Rat fist fight is unfair.

single_points.text: One reviewer says completing the last achievements, such as Frifle's challenges, killing 100 enemies with chandeliers, or searching for the Gunsling King, is a grindy, awful, and tedious experience.

citation.review_text:
I've had etg in my library, collecting dust, for abt a year and never really knew what i was missing. it isn't shocking to say that it was mostly inspired by tboi (and surely other roguelites), which is great, as i consider isaac to be one of my fav games oat. There's several mechanics which make isaac an amazing game that are shared with etg that result in them being so addictive and almost endless (etg to a lesser degree as it is far behind from tboi in terms of content).

The game was well structured with each chamber being unique, and having to craft the bullet to kill your past. I really enjoyed the bullet hell aspect of the game as it was balanced (for the most part) between fun and difficult +  its 'comedic'/nonsensical tropes within weapons, characters, story and dialogue which were pretty refreshing.

Now, i did not like how grindy the last achievements were. It was an awful and tedious experience completing Frifle's challenges / killing 100 enemies w/ chandeliers and I thought it was an unnecessary addition to the game. Same with searching for the 'gunsling king' iirc.

It's pretty tough to rank it compared to other games i've played, although I'll place it at 82.5/100

single_points.text: One reviewer says the dodge roll mechanic feels out of place and allows the composition of hazards to devolve into a lazy design mess.

citation.review_text:
Enter the Gungeon is polished, creative, and has awesome music.

However, I don't enjoy its combat.

My primary complaint is its dodge roll mechanic.  The studio loved the mechanic so much they named themselves after it, yet it feels completely out-of-place here.

Dodging can work well when it is primarily about global timing (tempo) and repositioning (burst of movement).  Dodge rolling isn't really either here.  Dodge rolling in Enter the Gungeon is an excuse for the designers to go crazy with the bullet hell and allow cases where it would be impossible to avoid being hit without invincibility frames.  Dodge rolling allows for the composition of hazards to devolve into a lazy design mess.

Earlier I said Enter the Gungeon is polished, but the composition of hazards is one area where the designers cut corners, and dodge roll is the main culprit for that.  If the game had lacked dodge rolling, it would have forced the designers to tighten how the hazards stack.

Another issue I have is with the RNG.  I rarely complain about RNG in roguelites.  However, Enter the Gungeon's gun RNG indirectly affects difficulty, mainly for bosses.   And the variance caused by RNG is whether or not bosses are a slog.  Especially in the early game, if the player is dealt low firepower, the boss battles drag on and on, and at least for me, that makes it more difficult because the battle strains my patience.

This is less of an issue in most other roguelites.  Sure, some RNG will result in faster and slower boss fights, but there's usually a steady average.

And part of it is Enter the Gungeon's dodge rolling, which I personally find exhausting, especially in boss fights, where I don't find it exhausting the way it is implemented in other games.

[h1]5/5 Perfectly wacky bullet-hell[/h1]
[h2]For how much content this game offers anything less than 5/5 would be shameful. I just wish there was more synergies with the unique guns but there are limitations when it comes to these things.[/h2]
[h2]Pros:[/h2]
[list]
[*]Tons of wacky weapons. (A shotgun that shoots shotgun shells, Skateboard gun, Unicorn horn, etc)
[*]Synergies for every weapon and passive items.
[*]Secret levels to find and extend your run. (One of them has a mini Punch out game)
[/list]
[h2]Cons:[/h2]
[list]
[*]Bad enemy hunt quest. (Spawn rates are abysmal for some of them taking forever to finish)
[/list]
[h2]Honestly I fail to find that many flaws with the game maybe I'm overlooking more obvious stuff but the game does feel a little bit like The binding of Isaac with it's synergy system, nothing wrong with it but if the game added more synergies then it might become more comparable. But I wouldn't mind this game being the baby's first Isaac game. The game does feel a little short with only 5 levels to go through but the secret levels and clone item does extend that.[/h2]
[h1]In conclusion. [url=https://youtu.be/xZzWiFjsbM0]Enter the gungeon[/url][/h1]

single_points.text: One reviewer says the early hours lack a compelling design, making progress difficult and frustrating until it clicks later on.

citation.review_text:
I was conflicted on how to rate this. But given my overall experience due to the game's addictive nature, I just have to recommend it. This is one of those games where you see yourself improve substantially the longer you play. While a lot of that is tied to the items you end up unlocking over the long run, there is a lot of muscle memory involved too. Memorizing attack patterns, knowing how to move and execute your dodge roll, focusing your fire on the enemy while simultanously evading bullet hell. It hits that sweet spot of being challenging enough to keep you engaged but not too difficult where you would lose interest.

I don't want to glaze this game too much as the deliberate design choice for the early hours isn't too compelling. It took me 3-4 attempts of returning to this game from a long break until I could fully commit to beating it. I hadn't made much progress for the first few hours, which had me frustrated. Upon doing some research, it appears many players had the same experience. While there is great gameplay waiting for you at the end of the tunnel, getting there is the real issue. Somewhere at around 20 hours, that's when it began to finally click for me. Comparing this to other games, it takes quite a lot of time to get fully invested.

While the game has a lot of RNG elements, some of which you’ll often end up at the mercy of, it seems to lack them in the areas where it would matter most. For instance, the rooms themselves are almost always identical when it comes to the enemies that spawn inside them. Enemies are very rarely randomized. And when they are, it’s usually just a few. This in combination with the fact that there is a finite amount of rooms, creates a repetitive nature that inevitably becomes a slog to get through.

And on the subject of RNG, it’s truly what screws you over the most. Not finding ammo, not finding keys, getting bad weapons from chests, not having the option to purchase a certain resource from the shopkeeper, etc. Granted…

single_points.text: One reviewer describes updates as making the game notably harder for new players with no benefits for them.

citation.review_text:
It's really hard for me to into words my feelings for this game.
It's a good game bogged down by committing to the bit too much.
There's a lot of guns. Too many guns, actually. And a lot of them are not very good.
There's some passive items, but they're rare. Rarer than their actual value, which almost makes them pointless.
It's difficult to play, difficult to make meaningful progress, difficult to put down, and difficult to actually enjoy.
It also got, like, reverse power-crept, where the game got updates that actually made it notably harder for new players with no benefits for them.

Update: After putting in an extra 60-something hours to finish the game, I do like it, but I still feel mostly the same overall. It's a good game, but makes a lot really questionable decisions that cause it to be rather annoying a lot of the time.
I do recommend playing the game casually, but I do not recommend trying to 100% the game. It's a slog.
